audit_rule: NOTHING counts as done until an adversarial round comes back clean AT THE GATE BELOW. Rewritten 2026-09-07 (AUDIT-RULE-V2) after Phase A ran SIX rounds without converging and Phase D took THIRTEEN. The intent is unchanged -- do not ship uncontrolled -- but the previous version could not terminate. Three defects, three fixes. || (1) THE GATE IS THE ONLY THING THAT COUNTS, AND THE REVIEWER IS TOLD SO. A finding blocks only if it can put a WRONG NUMBER in front of a user or on a broker order, or CORRUPT PERSISTED DATA. Everything else -- wording, comments, test hygiene, dead code, stale records, latent defects with no reachable path -- is not a finding for this purpose, and the audit brief must instruct the reviewer NOT TO REPORT IT AT ALL. Round 6 returned 16 findings of which 5 were real bugs; the other 11 cost triage time and are now recorded forever. An adversarial reviewer with no severity floor ALWAYS finds something, so 'clean' was unreachable by construction. || (2) THE TARGET SHRINKS, IT DOES NOT GROW. Round 1 reviews the whole change. Round N>1 reviews ONLY what changed since round N-1 -- the previous round's fixes -- plus any interaction those fixes have with already-reviewed code. Re-auditing the cumulative diff every round is what turned each round's fixes into the next round's findings: 9 of round 5's 15 findings sat in round 3-4 FIX CODE, including BOTH BLOCKING, while the original Phase A implementation produced ZERO BLOCKING across rounds 4 and 5. The feature was converging; the fixing was not. || (3) THE EXIT IS OBJECTIVE, NOT THE REVIEWER'S SILENCE. audit_clean is true when a round returns ZERO gate-level findings. Such a round triggers no fixes, so there is nothing new for a further round to look at -- and the round that reviewed the last batch of fixes was already the second look. One zero-finding round ends it. || HARD CAP: if a phase reaches THREE rounds without going clean, STOP AUDITING AND TELL KENNETH. (COUNTED PER STAGE -- decision AUDIT-CAP-PER-STAGE-2026-09-25: the PLAN rounds and the CODE rounds each have their own cap of three; a clean plan round closes the plan stage and the code stage starts at round 1 of 3. Phase records keep numbering rounds continuously, e.g. 'round 3 (code round 1)'.) That is evidence the batch is too big to audit, not that it needs a fourth round. || BATCH SIZE is the root cause the gate merely exposes. Phase A was 62 files across every layer of the app; nothing that size audits to clean. Split work so one change touches one layer, or roughly 500 lines. A change that size clears in one round. || FIXING: only gate-level findings are fixed in-branch. Nothing else -- not 'while I am here', not a one-line nit. Everything else is logged against main. Rounds 4 and 5 fixed 10 and 12 findings against a rule that already said this, and that non-compliance is a large part of why the loop stayed alive. || audit_rounds counts rounds RUN. A phase with status=shipped and audit_clean=false is NOT finished. This applies to `already_shipped` entries identically -- being written in that list means the CODE is done, never that the WORK is. || *** (1b) THE COMMENT-TRUTH EXCEPTION -- NARROWED, AND WRITTEN DOWN FOR THE FIRST TIME. Kenneth, 2026-09-22, answering pending_kenneth on AUTOTRADE-2B-MEASUREMENT-CORE: 'fix the rule, not the target'. *** Clause (1) above excludes 'wording, comments' from the gate, but PRACTICE HAD OPENED AN UNWRITTEN EXCEPTION TO IT: round 1 of the measurement core faulted F-5 on a comment claim, and from then on every round of that target counted comment claims as gate-level BY PRECEDENT, with no clause anywhere saying so and no bound on what qualified. UNBOUNDED, IT REPRODUCED AUDIT-RULE-V1'S NON-TERMINATION THROUGH THE ONE DOORWAY V2 LEFT OPEN -- three rounds, three findings, each an under-qualified claim inside the very comment written to correct the previous under-qualified claim (F-5 -> F2-1 -> F3-1). A dense docstring manufactures one finding per round forever, because each correction adds new prose carrying new claims. || THE EXCEPTION IS KEPT, BECAUSE A COMMENT THAT MISSTATES MECHANISM GETS ACTED ON, AND IT IS NOW BOUNDED: A COMMENT CLAIM IS GATE-LEVEL ONLY IF A COMPETENT READER, ACTING ON IT, WOULD WRITE A WRONG CHANGE -- i.e. only when it misstates MECHANISM: what the code does, which function is authoritative, what a guard is actually testing, which failure mode is live, or what is safe to change. THOSE STILL BLOCK, and the price-probe-versus-hours-test confusion that started this whole target is exactly one of them. || A COMMENT CLAIM IS *NOT* GATE-LEVEL when it is an ARITHMETIC WORKED-EXAMPLE, an ENUMERATION, or an ILLUSTRATIVE FIGURE inside a RESIDUALS, LIMITATIONS or WORKED-EXAMPLE block -- host-offset tables, DST hour counts, 'four hours daily', sample timestamps. Those ILLUSTRATE a mechanism stated elsewhere; they do not state it. PER CLAUSE (1), THE AUDIT BRIEF MUST INSTRUCT THE REVIEWER NOT TO REPORT THEM AT ALL. The one carve-back: if such a figure is wrong AND no correct statement of the mechanism appears nearby, the reader has nothing right to act on, so it IS a mechanism finding and blocks. THE TEST IS WHAT THE READER WOULD DO, NOT WHETHER THE ARITHMETIC CHECKS OUT. || THE TIEBREAK, so this is not re-litigated every round: IF A REVIEWER CANNOT DECIDE WHICH SIDE A CLAIM FALLS ON, IT IS NOT GATE-LEVEL -- log it against main, do not fix it in-branch. AND A PROSE FINDING NEVER BY ITSELF KEEPS A TARGET OPEN WHOSE BEHAVIOURAL AUDIT HAS ALREADY CONVERGED. || COROLLARY ON THE HARD CAP, which follows from the above and is flagged as an addition beyond the literal words Kenneth approved -- STRIKE THIS SENTENCE IF UNWANTED: the cap's stated reason is 'the batch is too big to audit'. WHEN A TARGET'S BEHAVIOURAL AUDIT HAS RETURNED ZERO GATE-LEVEL FINDINGS AND THE ONLY UNCONVERGED FINDINGS ARE PROSE, THE CAP'S USUAL REMEDY (SPLIT THE BATCH) IS A MISDIAGNOSIS. Say so and take it to Kenneth rather than splitting. Acting on a misdiagnosis is how a fifth split gets invented.

It passes the contract's OWN absolute `iv`, never `iv_rank` -- that variable holds a PERCENTILE whenever iv_basis=='rank', and a mutation feeding it is caught by the tests. Not-computed sorts to the end so an ungraded candidate cannot float to the top of a cheapest-stop-first sort. NO scanStore version bump, deliberately: the pair is additive and optional, an old blob's absent value collapses to null in cardToRow and renders 'not computed -- re-run the scan' (spec test 9), and a no-op migration branch would mislead the next reader. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not reading: six backend tests, five of which are mutation-tested (pricing at the flat invalidation, dropping the ATR guard, feeding the percentile as absolute IV, hardcoding PASS, and never attaching the gate -- ALL FIVE CAUGHT); 14 frontend tests. Both are now pinned in the fixture. Repriced at 0.35% vol, a contract reports almost its whole premium lost at any stop -- a confident, plausible, badly wrong CAUTION on every affected row, and a scan cannot 422 its way out of it. The scan now drops an out-of-band figure, logs it, and inverts the mid instead, which cannot disagree with the quote it came from. Two tests pin it (the suspect value must match the inverted-mid answer exactly, AND an in-band vendor IV must still change the answer -- otherwise the guard is a disguised iv=None), and removing the guard fails one of them. WHAT B3 DID NOT DO, per its decision: Phase C's piece 3 is untouched and `exit.invalidation` is not repointed. ---- B3 ROUNDS 1-2 (2026-09-08). ROUND 1: ONE gate-level finding, verified at file:line and reproduced numerically before fixing. The scan passed `contract["iv"]` into compute_stop_cost as iv_pct, commented as 'the contract's OWN absolute IV when the chain carried one'. FALSE whenever the ATM fill fired: on a chain with no vendor IV, the pre-existing block at scan.py:640 inverts the ATM mid and broadcasts that ONE number into every strike lacking an `iv`, so a 20-delta wing is handed the ATM's volatility. In-band, so the range guard could not catch it, and it flattens exactly the smile this gate exists to read. Supplying iv_pct also makes compute_stop_cost SKIP the mid inversion its own docstring calls the normal basis -- and that docstring names the hazard verbatim: 'a caller-supplied iv_pct need not reproduce the contract's own mid'. MEASURED (200/210C, 30 DTE, $4.41 mid, stop $192, Swing): the ATM's 25% prices 81% CAUTION where the contract's own mid gives 50% PASS -- 31 points and an INVERTED VERDICT, on the column the table sorts by. FIX (54ef1004): iv_pct=None unconditionally. The gate is `loss = premium - BS(stop,K,T,r,iv)`, which only subtracts like from like when the volatility reproduces the very mid `premium` came from; inversion guarantees that by construction, any supplied number can only break it. The out-of-band range guard went with it -- it sanitised an argument no longer passed, and a guard that could not catch the in-band case it was aimed at was never the protection it appeared to be. TESTS: two existing tests pinned the REMOVED behaviour, one asserting an in-band `iv` MUST change the answer -- the defect written down as a contract. WHAT C1 DID: the stock stop every trade card is built around is now the wider of the structural level and a 2xATR floor, resolved ONCE per symbol in `resolve_stock_stop` (scoring/exit_plan.py) and RECEIVED by `build_trade_plan` as a required `final_stop_price` keyword. `exit.invalidation` carries that number; a new `exit.finalStop` block (FinalStopOut: price, source, stopSource, structuralSource, structuralPrice, atrFloorPrice, distanceDollar, atr, computedAt) carries its provenance so the 'Bottom (final stop)' row can render before Compute Arithmetic Plan is ever pressed. On that path there is no structural level and no ATR floor to report, so NO finalStop block is sent and the ranking badge refuses to price: 'not computed', never a block of nulls that reads as 'we looked and found nothing'. Both halves pinned in test_scan_endpoint.py::test_scan_rr_bullish_invalidation_pct_override_bites_only_on_a_dead_feed -- inert on a real feed (so nobody 'fixes' it back into a live flat stop), live on a dead one (so a user-visible execution parameter has not gone silently dead). || /contracts/recompute-plan ECHOES the card's own finalStop rather than re-deriving one. `mergePlan` replaces `exit` wholesale, so an endpoint returning no stop would wipe finalStop and drop invalidation back to a flat percentage for exactly the cards a user hand-picked a contract on. A fresh candle fetch was the first draft and was WRONG twice over: it adds a network round trip to an interactive endpoint whose stated design is 'one contract's fields in the body, no chain', and a feed that has moved on since the scan would hand back a DIFFERENT stop -- the override silently moving the level, which is the failure part 3 exists to prevent. The stop is a STOCK level; which contract is traded has no bearing on where structure sits. || STILL OUTSTANDING (C2, frontend): plan section 5 parts 3-half, 4 and the card rendering. `finalStop` on the wire type; the 'Bottom (final stop)' row reading it before an Arithmetic Plan exists, with contract-priced sub-cells and recommendedSize at '--' (part 2); mergePlan/withCachedEstimate keeping the block across a Step 6 override; and the scanStore migration -- NOTE THE PLAN IS STALE HERE, it says 'v12 -> 13' and the store is at version 14, so the bump is 14 -> 15. || PART 5 (the ranking badge) IS ALREADY DONE and needs no work: B3 shipped exactly what it specifies -- two fields on WatchlistRow (stopCostPct/stopCostStatus), populated in cardToRow, one grid track in COLUMNS and TableRow. Verified 2026-09-09, do not rebuild it. || Backend on C1: 2150 passed, 1 skipped. RECONCILES rather than merely being green -- main stood at 2132, test_stock_stop_resolution.py adds 15 and test_scan_endpoint.py nets +3 (one flat-override test replaced by four), test_trade_plan.py nets 0 (four flat-percentage tests replaced by four received-stop ones). || C2 (frontend). `TradeCardData.exit.finalStop` carries the provenance and `exit.invalidation` became `number | null`. The 'Bottom (final stop)' row now renders FROM THE SCAN before Compute Arithmetic Plan is ever pressed -- price, both candidates and the gap between them, plus the justification prose -- with 'Contract value at stop' and 'Max loss if stopped' printed as '--' rather than omitted (part 2: an absent row reads as 'there is no such thing', a dash reads as 'not computed yet'), and the risk-derived size already returned null without a plan so it needed no change. || SCANSTORE v14 -> v15, NOT 12 -> 13: the plan file is STALE on that number, the store had moved to 14 under Phase A. NOT cosmetic: `buildPaperPosition` stores that field as `PortfolioPosition.stop`, the level STOP_REACHED fires against, so a user ordering from a restored candidate would arm a -3% stop believing it structural, up to 3x tighter than the level the app now claims a position's stop is. The branch is IDEMPOTENT (it skips any candidate that already has a block), which v13's own history says matters: that branch was edited nine commits after shipping and had to be re-run under a new version. || null renders 'not computed -- re-run the scan' on the Invalidation field (EditableKV gained a `nullLabel`; a bare dash beside an editable dollar field reads as zero) and fails `checkInvalidation`, so `missing_invalidation` blocks the send -- a branch that was EFFECTIVELY UNREACHABLE before piece 3, since the scan always sent a number. Two knock-ons that were NOT in the plan and are defects if skipped: (1) `checkTradeRisk` gained an optional `resolvedInvalidation`, threaded from step 7's `invalidationFor` through a new `invalidationBySymbol` prop on SendToBrokerDialog -- reading `card.exit.invalidation` alone would refuse a restored card FOREVER, even after the user typed a stop, which is the one gesture that fixes it; (2) `estimateFirstPassage` bails when the resolved stop is null, because `estimate_stock_first_passage` gates the stop leg on `invalidation_price > 0` and would have answered a probability of invalidation of ZERO -- read on screen as 'this trade cannot be stopped out'. When a response carries no block the card's is kept ALONG WITH ITS `invalidation` -- keeping the block while letting a flat-fallback number through would print a structural provenance row above a stop it does not describe. When both carry one the PLAN wins, because the plan's `invalidation` was computed against the plan's block and a mismatched pair is worse than either half. || Frontend on C2: typecheck clean, 111 suites / 1367 tests. phases.name: Piece 4 -- per-position premium stop
phases.note: Built and green. TWO adversarial rounds run, NEITHER clean. Round 1 found 8 defects (all fixed). Round 2 found 8 more in this phase alone, all fixed: the frontend PREMIUM_STOP copied only one of the backend's two guards, so a failed quote (currentPrice coerced to 0) fired a Critical toast for EVERY position on every 30s cycle with no backend alert behind it -- a regression the pnlPct test it replaced did not have; the card displayed one premium stop and posted another, twice over (the reset re-seeds the field without telling the parent cache, and mergePlan swaps `exit` under an overridden card without changing `contract` so nothing re-runs -- the second reproduced the 78% stop that round 1 was supposed to have killed); a dollar stop at or beyond the entry fell back silently and also discarded a valid client-sent fraction; the drawer cleared the override on any entry >= 100 and persisted every keystroke, so typing '45' armed a 4% stop; the server-derived fraction was dropped from the create response, leaving the two engines disagreeing until the next sync; a dead schema field; and two tests that asserted plumbing while claiming to cover behaviour -- the router derivation and the PATCH write had NO test, and now go through the endpoint. NOT YET CLEAN -- round 3 pending. || ROUND 3 (combined, all three items at once) found 14 more and every one was fixed; audit_clean stays FALSE until a round comes back clean. The CRITICAL was the same display-vs-posted split round 2 thought it had closed, reached by REVERSING the order of the two events: an unrelated edit BEFORE a mergePlan caches the old seed, the re-seed effect then moves the field without telling the parent, and premiumStopDollarToSend compared the stale cache against the NEW seed and let it through -- card showing $0.80 while $1.50 was posted. Root cause was inferring touched-ness by comparing values; it is now TRACKED and threaded to the page via onEditsChange's meta.touched.premiumStop, which also fixes the mirror defect (a user who typed the seed's own value back had the choice discarded). Also: the offline-retry path in syncFromBackend dropped the server-derived premiumStopPct, leaving the two engines disagreeing; the auto-trader test asserted the resolver directly and never called fire() or _check_daily_loss, so BOTH call sites could be reverted with 75 tests still green (replaced with two that drive the service and fail on that mutation); entryPrice had no gt=0 so a non-positive entry silently dropped the user's dollar stop unlogged; the drawer rewrote a stored stop on a bare focus-and-blur (0.4843 rendered '48' and committed 0.48) and could not represent sub-1% or >=99.5% fractions at all; and the persisted store gained two fields with no version bump (now v3). ROUND 5 (11 findings, all fixed): the badge percentage came from the printed pair while the badge's COLOUR and tooltip (`status`) still came from full precision, so at a 0.70 pass line $1.77 away x 0.789 on a $2.00 premium printed '70% OF PREMIUM' in PASS green above an equation that hand-checks to exactly 70% (~0.18% of ordinary inputs) -- the verdict now comes from the same printed pair, via one shared printedFrom(); a sub-cent premium produced a card of four contradictory zeroes ('0%' badge, total-loss tooltip, '$0 of $0 premium') and now returns null into the existing N/A path; PremiumStopEditor's two REVERT paths returned without clearing dirtyRef, so typing 100, blurring, then merely clicking in and out PATCHed a live stop nobody touched -- round 4's defect re-entered through the rejected-edit path; lastStoredRef's 'never while the user is mid-edit' was asserted but not implemented (a 30s sync overwrote typing); FastAPI's `detail` is a LIST for a validation 422 and all four parse sites cast it to string, so entryPrice's new gt=0 bound could crash the whole Portfolio page via detail.split(); the card's premium-stop field was min=0.01 with no max, so typing 0 -- the natural way to say 'no override' -- clamped to $0.01 and pinned a 0.19% stop (Critical alert on the first cent of adverse move, and a ~3000x cut to the auto-trader's daily-loss denominator), now bounded to 10-99% of the mid to match the global's own ge=0.10 bound; the router's live-quote guard tested the RAW quote and rounded after, so a $0.004 quote stored entry_price 0.0, which alert_generator's `entry_price > 0` gate makes permanently unable to raise a stop alert; the Alerts page rendered the resolved stop through Math.round, reprinting the exact 0%/100% lossiness premiumStop.ts documents as fixed; and AutoTradeArm's doc comment claimed arming and sending 'cannot arm a position at two different stops' when they share only the DOLLAR by design. ROUND 6 (11 findings; 10 fixed, 1 escalated to Kenneth): round 5's own 10-99%-of-mid bounds RE-OPENED the stray-click defect rounds 4 and 5 closed -- EditableKV.save clamps BEFORE its no-op guard, so when the SEED sits outside the bounds the clamp alone makes next !== value and a bare focus-and-blur reports a deliberate edit; the seed is round(mid x global, 2) and the global is allowed up to 1.0, at which point 1951 of 2000 mids from $0.01-$20.00 seed above the max. Now guarded on the PRE-CLAMP draft, with a test verified to fail without it. Also: the badge dropped the schematic's verdict word (StatusBadge renders `label ?? STATUS_LABEL`, so a supplied label REPLACES it), leaving colour as the only thing separating two badges that both print '70% of premium' with opposite verdicts -- the word is back and leads the badge, matching the schematic; the sub-cent guard tested the ROUNDED premium and (0.005).toFixed(2) rounds UP to 0.01, so it never rejected the case it was written for (now on the raw premium, and its test no longer claims 0.005 is 'exactly one cent'); the drawer's 'Fires at premium $X' rounded half-up while both engines compare at full precision, advertising a price that fires nothing (now floored); the two engines wrote position_alert_history reference_value at two precisions; two assertions compared literals to literals and could not fail; and three comments asserted live failure paths that the render gate, the schema bound and market.py respectively foreclose. || ROUNDS 7 AND 8 were recorded only in their commit messages (c39eb7e5, 05627fa1) and never here, under a green state.py -- a presence probe cannot see a missing narrative. Round 7: 17 findings, 15 fixed, 1 rejected on arithmetic, 1 recorded; the trade-affecting ones were the Monte Carlo and its staleness guard still falling back to data.exit.invalidation while the position is stopped at overlay.invalidation, the Invalidation field becoming PortfolioPosition.stop with no bound or directional check, roundCents's Number.EPSILON nudge being arithmetically inert above ~$2 (2999 of 4,995,000 pairs mis-rounded, moving the VERDICT), handleEditsChange early-returning on a null contract key so a typed limit was displayed and dropped, and the three edit caches surviving a setScanResult. Round 8: 13 findings, 11 fixed, 1 rejected after building it, 1 partly deferred; the CRITICAL was the Entry limit reaching the broker unbounded, and finding 4 was a REGRESSION from round 7's own fix (<input type='number'> sanitizes any half-typed literal to '', which round 7 had made mean 'revert to inheriting'). || ROUND 9 (17 findings: 1 CRITICAL, 4 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM-HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 1 LOW-MEDIUM, 5 LOW) -- all 17 fixed, and audit_clean STAYS FALSE until a round comes back clean. The CRITICAL was reached through the one path nobody had looked at, the SERVER: portfolio.py re-anchors `stop` by (live - scanStockPrice) so a plan level still sits the right distance from the underlying, and this branch made that field a price the USER TYPES -- round 8 even bounded it against the live quote -- so $180 typed on a $200 stock scanned at $145 stored $235, ABOVE spot, raising a Critical STOP_REACHED with Gmail and Telegram behind it on the first backend scan. A new `stopIsUserSet` flag exempts only `stop`. Also: the optimistic row adopted the server's premiumStopPct while keeping the CLIENT's entryPrice, so the two engines compared `price <= entry * (1 - pct)` against different entries (a $3.12 stop filled at $4.00 became $4.06 locally) -- which is also why round 7's rejection of the entry-limit finding did not cover it: that identity holds only when ONE entry is used for both derivation and threshold; at the EXACT pass line the badge said PASS above an equation hand-checking to CAUTION, because round 5 moved the verdict onto the printed pair and then compared it with a float quotient (0.16/0.20 is 0.7999999999999999), now cross-multiplied in integer cents; a half-typed decimal COMMITTED a truncation (parseFloat('2.') is 2, Number('48.') is 48), so round 8 had traded 'reverts to a value the user didn't choose' for 'commits a value the user didn't choose' and only the second reaches a broker; AutoTradeArm still anchored entry_premium on the scan-time mid, mis-sizing the backend daily-loss gate by 2.4x on a stale scanResult; the backend never got round 8's bounds at all (limit_price now gt=0 on all three order schemas, and a user-set stop on the wrong side of the live underlying is now a 422); the 'premium stop could not be applied' notice covered 2 of 4 create paths and the two that had it overwrote each other's note; the Barrier Race simulated an UNTOUCHED seed against the fresh premium and labelled it 'from the editable field above'; and the reject-don't-clamp policy gave no feedback at all, which a test now pins. Four test/doc defects: the spec-8 two-send-path test was a TAUTOLOGY (one pure function called twice with one argument, the results compared to each other) in the block whose header calls it 'the mandated test that shipped missing' -- replaced with a page-level test driving Place Limit and a basket submit, verified to fail when only the basket path is reverted; round 6's Math.floor on the drawer preview was unpinned (mutating it to Math.round left all 69 tests green); two doc blocks on the bounds were ORPHANED and both asserted the opposite of their code; and AGENTS.md kept the overstated state.py claim that round 7 corrected in CLAUDE.md. || ROUND 11 (report-only, the first under AUDIT-EXIT-CRITERION-2026-09-05): 17 findings, TWO classed GATE-BLOCKING and fixed, 15 classed FOLLOW-UP and NOT fixed in-branch. Both gate-blocking findings were the same root cause in EditDrawer's EditField, and finding 1 was a regression introduced by dea3f943 -- round 10's own commit, which no round had reviewed. EditField was a fully controlled <input type='number'> with no draft, committing every keystroke; round 10 added a magnitude range that returns WITHOUT calling onChange when out of range. Together those make typing impossible and the failure mode is a DELETED stop: Number('') === 0, the range exempts 0, and both Stop call sites map 0 to null. Retyping a $140 stop as 130 on a $145 underlying (range [29, 435]) deletes the stop on the clear, then rejects 1 and 13 as below the floor, and lands on null with the warning wiped by the trailing 0. Executed: with the range disabled the same keystrokes yield 130; with it, null. It is money, not usability -- both alert engines gate STOP_REACHED on the stop existing (alertEngine.ts's `stop != null`, alert_generator.py's `pos.stop is not None`), so the position can never raise a stop alert again while the user believes they just set one. Structural stop has identical wiring and does it to STRUCTURAL_STOP_BREACHED. Finding 2 was the second half: type='number' sanitizes '132.' to '', so merely typing the decimal point of 132.50 produced the same empty string and the same deleted stop -- verbatim round 8's finding, fixed then in TradeCard's EditableKV and PremiumStopEditor and never carried to the two fields holding PortfolioPosition.stop itself. FIX: EditField is now draft-then-commit on type='text' inputMode='decimal', the pattern PremiumStopEditor in the same file reached across rounds 4-5 -- keystrokes move a local draft, the range is judged once on commit, a complete-decimal-literal check rejects a trailing point, a blur without typing writes nothing, and an EMPTY draft REVERTS with a message rather than clearing (an explicit 0 remains the documented clear). Round 10's three range tests fired ONE change carrying the complete final string -- the paste gesture, the only one the per-keystroke range did not break -- which is how this shipped green; three new tests drive a LIVE parent that merges the patch and simulate TYPING, and all three were verified to fail against the old component (the first reporting two writes where there should be one). Frontend 103 suites / 1215 tests, typecheck silent. || ROUND 13 (report-only, first round to CLEAR the gate): GATE 0, FOLLOW-UP 10. The auditor wrote no code, per ROUND-12-REPORT-ONLY. It re-derived round 12's premiumStopFiringPrice independently over 1,994,149 (entry, whole-cent dollar stop) pairs and confirmed it returns exactly the greatest 2dp price <= entry*(1-pct) with no off-by-one in either direction, and checked the stop-cost notation's mutual consistency over 783,000 (premium, move, delta) triples -- badge percent, dollars-left, headline, printed equation, PASS/CAUTION word and total-loss tooltip all agree and the headline always sums. A live jest probe drove the real Step 7 page through edit -> Next -> Prev -> Place Limit and confirmed the posted premiumStopDollar matches the displayed one. Baselines matched exactly: typecheck silent, 103 suites / 1218 tests, backend 2004 passed / 1 skipped. The ten follow-ups are in round_13_followups, logged against main.

phases.note: BUILT AND CLEAN AFTER 2 ROUNDS on branch claude/iv-basis-phase-c-7mimv4, PUSHED and UNMERGED -- merging is Kenneth's call, as every merge so far has been. || BRANCH NAME: that branch had already been merged (Phase C, at 430bdb24) and was RESTARTED from origin/main under the same name rather than branched afresh, because the session's harness rules name it as the designated branch and prescribe exactly that for a merged branch. phases.name: Heston pricer -- Fourier inversion (Q8)
phases.note: F1 (THE PRICER) IS BUILT on claude/dev-state-reconstruction-hzmzbi at cf3da087 plus the round-1 audit fixes. Spec: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-heston-calibration-spec.md, and READ ITS SECTION 0a FIRST -- the build falsified two of the spec's own claims. || WHAT WAS WRONG: heston_price's _integrand re-applied exp(i*phi*lnS)/exp(i*phi*lnK) on top of a characteristic function that already carried e^{i*phi*ln(S/K)}. The moneyness exponents collected to 2i*phi*ln(S/K) + j*ln(S/K): a DOUBLED Fourier frequency plus a spurious (S/K)^j on P1, which also never divided by the Bakshi-Madan normaliser f2(-i)=S*e^{rT}. Error exactly zero at K==S (why it survived), +451% at 45 DTE and +2782% at 180 DTE in the |delta| 0.15-0.90 band scan.py ranks. _heston_char_fn was and is CORRECT and was NOT touched. || VERIFIED, not asserted: against an independently written reference (the two-CF form reaching P1 via b1=kappa-rho*sigma, u1=+1/2 rather than the Bakshi-Madan shift) the corrected pricer agrees to 0.000000% over 112 points, 7-365 DTE x 140-275 strikes. sigma_v->0 collapse to Black-Scholes: worst 0.0139% over 46 points, where the old code failed by 83161%. It is also 1.24-1.36x FASTER (test_heston_perf's realistic chain 0.56s -> 0.35s) because the correct integrand needs fewer quad subdivisions. || THE GATE-LEVEL NUMBER: on test_trade_plan's _plan() fixture (spot 318.73, K 375, 185 DTE, premium 7.47) the exit premium falls 12.52 -> 3.80 and the displayed R/R FLIPS +1.13 -> -0.82. The card was recommending, at +1.13, a trade whose first target leaves the position under water. || READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING ANY 'Heston repriced' NUMBER: F1 DOES NOT MAKE THE CARD RIGHT. It fixes the pricer; v0_grid=[0.04] is untouched until F2. Measured on the spec's reference chain with the shipped reduced grid through the POST-F1 pricer: rel-RMSE 0.645 at 45 DTE against a flat-BS baseline of 0.197 (3.27x WORSE than one flat volatility) and 0.754 vs 0.563 at 180 DTE (1.34x worse). Per strike, post-F1 Heston sits 27% to 100% BELOW the market mid across the whole band. scan.py still accepts method=='heston_grid' and labels it 'Heston repriced'. So the defect's DIRECTION flipped (wrong HIGH -> wrong LOW) and F1 is still a large net improvement, because the pricer error it removes dwarfs the calibration error it leaves -- but F2 IS NOT OPTIONAL POLISH, it is the other half of one defect, and its section 3.3 baseline gate is what makes shipping a fit seven times worse than a flat vol impossible. || SCOPE GREW BY ONE MEASURED DEFECT during the audit, and it is in F1's own stated scope (the two quad calls): the spec's 'the quadrature limits (500, limit=100) are measured sufficient' is FALSE. The integrands decay as exp(-0.5*v*T*phi^2), so the needed cutoff scales as 1/sqrt(v*T); a fixed 500 is 0.769% wrong at v0=0.01, theta=0.02, 1 DTE at the money. Reachable: v0=0.01 is in the grid under HESTON_FULL_CALIBRATION, heston_chain passes weeklies, and F2's chain seeding reaches it by default on a low-IV underlying. Now adaptive: min(max(500, sqrt(50/(v*T))), 20000) at v=min(v0,theta), limit=200. Worst error over 324 cases 0.769% -> 0.00218%, at 1.00x latency (the formula returns <500 for every expiry at the production default v0=theta=0.04). This also cut the worst out-of-band below-forward-intrinsic shortfall 0.127316 -> 0.002235; the two were one defect. || SIX existing tests pinned pricer output, NOT the four the spec's section 5.3 listed. Two lost their premise entirely (their fixtures no longer produce the 'artifact' dip, because the dip WAS this bug) and are renamed: test_estimate_targets_real_fixture_preserves_t3_after_t2_artifact -> ..._ladder_is_clean_and_all_heston, and test_trade_plan's test_heston_params_floors_non_monotonic_target_instead_of_falling_back -> test_heston_params_thread_through_to_a_clean_all_heston_ladder. THE rho FLIP IS WHY THE SKEWED-PARAMETER TESTS EXIST: the spec's section 5.1 as written pinned the pricer only where it degenerates to Black-Scholes, so inverting rho -- destroying the entire skew -- passed every test in it. Confirmed pytest-asyncio 0.23.8's event_loop fixture closes without cancelling tasks and _chain_future._call_set_state silently drops a result for a closed loop; old file with fakes slowed fails 4/4, new passes 3/3; both slowed files in one run -> the new leak test catches the old file's leaked task (cross-test mechanism); new file 5/5 under 6 CPU burners; mutant (done-callback removed) killed; no other test has the pattern; 'not a production leak' sound. Non-blocking folded in: N1 wording -- the failing test is the first LATER test with gc.collect()+caplog (3 tests sit between), and a leaked task also holds a _HESTON_SEMAPHORE permit (could also have failed holds_semaphore_until_real_completion); N2 the concurrency-limit test now also awaits the helper; N4 redundant current_task() filter removed. CAUSE: test_process_symbol_falls_back_when_calibration_exceeds_timeout abandons a calibration whose fake takes 0.5s, then waited a FIXED asyncio.sleep(0.5) -- ~50ms of margin. Under full-suite load the executor thread finishes after the sleep, pytest-asyncio closes the function-scoped loop with the task still pending at scan.py:361 (awaiting run_in_executor), the late thread result is dropped (loop closed), and the task is later finalized as 'Task was destroyed but it is pending!' -- an asyncio ERROR that the NEXT test, test_abandoned_heston_task_exception_does_not_leak_unretrieved, collects with gc.collect() and fails its no-asyncio-ERROR caplog assertion. NOT A PRODUCTION LEAK: the abandoned task is strongly held via the executor future's callback until the thread finishes, and production's loop lives for the whole process. REPRO: the old timeout test with its trailing sleep cut to 0.3s (a synthetic 0.2s delay) fails the next test with the exact logged message; with both fakes slowed 0.4s, old tests fail, new tests pass. FIX: new helper _await_abandoned_heston_calibrations() waits (bounded 10s, asserting none left) for every _run_heston_calibration task on the test's loop, used in place of both fixed sleeps. Centred on its trigger, it pushed 110px past each edge into the nearest scrolling ancestor, on every badge carrying a tooltip, permanently. That was the single cause of every 'constant' horizontal scrollbar in the screener -- overflow that did not move when the viewport doubled, because it was a fixed 220px box and not a proportion. IDENTIFIED BY ARITHMETIC, not by inspection: predicted 110 + half the trigger, measured Step 5's GATE badge 80px -> 150, SymbolHeader 70px -> 145 and 64px -> 142. Three predictions, three exact matches. Fixed with `display: none` + transition-behavior allow-discrete + @starting-style, which keeps the fade and costs no accessibility that `visibility: hidden` had not already taken. Step 5 and Step 7 went from 58px and 60-101px of overflow to zero AT REST at 1440 and 1920. CORRECTED BY ROUND 1, and the correction matters: `display: none` did not REMOVE that overflow, it moved it to HOVER TIME. Measured on step 5's .stepBody (overflow-x: auto): scrollWidth 1350 at rest, 1408 while the GATE badge is hovered -- the same 58px, back. The headless browser used overlay scrollbars so nothing moved; on a desktop Chrome with classic scrollbars a horizontal bar appears under the cursor and steals ~15px of height, so the table shifts vertically whenever the user points at a badge and settles back when they leave. A scrollbar that appears BECAUSE you pointed at something is worse than a constant one. The Step 7 half of the original claim was never verifiable either way: that page renders its empty state without a picked contract and a live backend. Both are open -- see the deferred tooltip-portal item. || RANKING TABLE, step-4-ranking: headings named the WRONG COLUMNS whenever the table was too narrow to fit. A bare `1fr` is `minmax(auto, 1fr)` and collapses to MIN-CONTENT when the grid has no slack -- the header's min-content is the word 'NAME' (30.375px measured), every row's is 0px (.nameCell clips), so from HORIZON rightward each heading sat exactly 30px clear of its own data. Silent, invisible on a wide screen, invisible to every test. Now minmax(100px, 1fr); the 100 floor is what makes the laptop's horizontal scroll honest (under minmax(0,1fr) you would scroll right to uncover SCORE and STOP while the company names stayed at zero width). Panel went 40% -> 58%/814px -> 48% after Kenneth rejected the middle one on sight for crushing the chart to 522px; 48% with every fixed track trimmed (530 -> 418px) and the gap cut 12 -> 8px fits all TEN columns and returns the chart to 687px at 1920, against 795px in the original layout. Laptop width scrolls, Kenneth's own choice over stacking. HORIZON survives as 'HRZN' -- it is a CONSTANT (cardToRow reads it from the scan context, so every row of a scan is identical and the top bar already shows it); dropping it would give the chart another 52px and is offered, not taken. || STEP 5 BANNER now says WHY the gate reads as it does, counting drivers across the rows and keeping 'no volatility reading' SEPARATE from 'IV failed its threshold' -- same CAUTION badge, opposite meanings, and on this app the missing reading is the common case. The IV column heading is now derived from the bases on screen (ivColumnLabel: 'IV' / 'IV RANK' / 'IV / IV RANK') because a column headed 'IV' under a banner saying 'IV rank <= 34' reads as two quantities, and there are genuinely THREE on that screen. || VERIFICATION NOTE worth keeping: an intermediate check reported '0 overflowing' on all eight page/width combinations and was nearly believed. Tests in backend/tests/test_state_audit_bookkeeping.py drive a real temporary git repo rather than mocking subprocess, because both defects were about which value reached git; all three defect-restoring mutants are killed. || ROUND 1 (2026-09-16) RETURNED FOUR GATE-LEVEL FINDINGS, all fixed in-branch. (1) With neither origin/main nor main resolving -- a --single-branch or --depth 1 clone -- the probe returned None, which renders as "No drift": a clean bill for a check that never ran, the very observable this change exists to remove. It now WARNS that it could not look, at exit 0, since git being unavailable is not evidence of drift. (2) THE SHARPEST: the round number was taken over the WHOLE branch while the pointer resolves ONE piece, so a branch carrying two pieces answered for the earlier piece's rounds -- a red banner on an entirely honest file whose printed remedy ("record the count there") could only be satisfied by writing a number known to be false into this file. _pointer_scoped_base now walks the state file's own history and stops where active_phase last differed. (3) Preferring origin/main outright was wrong for this project's own workflow: it merges with a local --no-ff and pushes afterwards, and pushes from these containers have 403'd, so between merge and push origin/main is the STALE ref and the merge route out of the banner did not work. The base is now whichever candidate yields the fewest commits in ref..HEAD. (4) This entry's own verify probe pinned UNPHASED_FAIL_ROUND, a constant belonging to dead-end #2, so the entire revival could be reverted while state.py still certified it shipped -- the same modelling error STATE_TRACKING.md already names about v0_grid. The commit that MOVES the pointer therefore stayed inside the new pointer's range -- and recording the round that just finished while moving the pointer is ONE commit in this repo's actual style ("Record round 4: clean at the gate...", "Phase G is in: name the merge, clear the active phase", "The bearish gate is in: name the merge, clear the branch"). A piece with zero rounds of its own drew red DRIFT for the previous piece's round number, clearable only by merging or by writing a false count. The walk now takes the OLDEST commit still carrying the pointer -- the one that set it -- and excludes it. Round 2 also proved the round-1 test pinned the defect rather than the behaviour, which is why that assertion was rewritten rather than kept. Four of round 2's below-gate items were inside the function being rewritten and were fixed with it: the (ref, detail) contract was only true on failure, the unborn-HEAD diagnosis blamed a clone flag, json.loads caught only ValueError so a non-object state file would traceback the SessionStart hook, and exhausting _POINTER_SCAN_LIMIT degraded to the FULL range -- back to the pre-fix false positive rather than to something safe. || ROUND 3 (2026-09-16) RETURNED ONE GATE-LEVEL FINDING, again inside the PREVIOUS ROUND'S FIX -- the third round running without going clean, which is audit_rule's HARD CAP: STOP AUDITING AND TELL KENNETH. When active_phase TRANSITIONS to null inside the range, round 2's boundary change (take the OLDEST commit still carrying the pointer and EXCLUDE it) collapses the range to empty -- the clearing commit is the newest state-file commit, so it becomes the boundary and is excluded, leaving `git log HEAD..HEAD`. The UNPHASED path then never runs, and that path's entire premise is that rounds are running and NOTHING in the file counts them: it is the path this whole revival exists to restore. The third option -- ask whether ANY already_shipped entry accounts for the rounds -- is the comparison audit_bookkeeping_drift's own docstring rejects as useless, because Phase D's 13 rounds are a global maximum nothing can exceed. || REACHABILITY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: this repo has never cleared the pointer on a branch. Four options were put to Kenneth: (1) declare clean on the behavioural gate and merge; (2) grant one round 4 scoped to the F3-1 fix alone; (3) narrow the comment-truth exception in audit_rule so it counts only claims about mechanism a reader could act on wrongly, not arithmetic worked-examples in a residuals block -- the fix to the RULE rather than to the target; (4) cut the docstring down. decisions.a: *** KENNETH TOOK THE RECOMMENDATION, 2026-09-22: (3) THEN (1) -- 'fix the rule, not the target.' His gloss is verbatim from option (3)'s own text, which is how the reading was confirmed. *** || (3) IS DONE: audit_rule now carries clause (1b), THE FIRST WRITTEN STATEMENT OF THE COMMENT-TRUTH EXCEPTION, and it is bounded. Gate-level only if a competent reader ACTING ON THE CLAIM would write a wrong change -- misstated MECHANISM: what the code does, which function is authoritative, what a guard tests, which failure mode is live, what is safe to change. NOT gate-level: arithmetic worked-examples, enumerations and illustrative figures inside residuals/limitations blocks, which the brief must tell the reviewer not to report at all. Carve-back: a wrong figure with NO correct mechanism statement nearby IS a mechanism finding. Tiebreak: undecidable means NOT gate-level, logged against main. || WHY THE RULE AND NOT THE TARGET, which is the whole point and must not be lost: the exception was never written down. It existed only as PRECEDENT from round 1 faulting F-5, with no bound on what qualified, and unbounded it reproduced AUDIT-RULE-V1'S NON-TERMINATION through the one doorway v2 left open. Patching the docstring (option 4) or granting round 4 (option 2) would have cleared this target and left the next dense docstring to do it again. || (1) IS DONE: AUTOTRADE-2B-MEASUREMENT-CORE is audit_clean TRUE, status shipped, audit_rounds 3. THE BASIS IS ROUND 2 RE-READ UNDER (1b) -- its only finding was a host-offset worked-example, which (1b) excludes, so round 2 is a ZERO-GATE-LEVEL round and that is audit_rule (3)'s objective exit. Not an assertion of clean; a round that already met the exit once the rule was corrected. || DISCLOSED, NOT BURIED: commit 3859220e (the F3-1 prose fix) IS UNAUDITED, and under (1b) it does not owe a round because a residuals-block prose edit is not gate surface. Both prose commits are comment-only with the suite byte-identical at 2811/1. || THE CAP COROLLARY IS AN ADDITION BEYOND KENNETH'S LITERAL WORDS AND IS FLAGGED AS SUCH IN (1b) WITH A STRIKE INSTRUCTION: when the behavioural audit has returned zero and only prose is unconverged, the cap's 'split the batch' remedy is a MISDIAGNOSIS. It is load-bearing for (1) -- declaring clean after a fired cap requires saying why the cap does not mean what it usually means -- so it is written down rather than left implicit. Strike the sentence if unwanted; nothing else depends on it. || *** WHAT THIS CLEAN DOES NOT COVER: F-1's accepted cost. The common nightly-ingested path is still knowingly mismatched after 16:00 ET. THE STAMP ON THE SNAPSHOT TARGET CLOSES IT and supersedes guard (i). A clean behavioural gate is not the exposure being gone. *** || MERGING IS NOT DONE. Option (1)'s text says 'declare it clean AND MERGE'. The declaration is done here; THE MERGE TO MAIN IS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN UNATTENDED -- every merge in this project's record is an explicit act by Kenneth on stated evidence, and he asked for a handoff rather than a merge in the same breath. It is the next action, not a forgotten one. || *** THE 'COMMENT-ONLY' CLAIM IS NOW PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE UNAUDITED COMMIT SAFE TO ACCEPT: `auto_trader.py` was parsed at 4a286e18 and at 3859220e, every docstring stripped from Module/FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/ClassDef bodies, and the two ASTs compared -- THEY ARE IDENTICAL. So dcff1667 and 3859220e changed NO EXECUTABLE LINE WHATSOEVER, and 3859220e being unaudited cannot move a number, a broker order or persisted data BY CONSTRUCTION, not merely by a reviewer's reading. Re-run: parse both revisions, strip docstrings, compare ast.dump. ***

decisions.q: Round 1 of the measurement core FALSIFIED the premise the guard (i) decision rests on. That decision says '(i) closes the narrow one WITHOUT GIVING THE COMMON ONE BACK'; historical_store.py:230 says otherwise. Three resolutions were put to Kenneth: (1) revert 4b273f22's trim to unconditional, keep the honest premise (guard (ii)), then build the stamp -- restores the match on the COMMON path and accepts the narrower stale-DB break; (2) skip the interim and build the stamp NOW -- gate matches scan by construction on both paths, but it touches the arm path and so widens this target; (3) KEEP guard (i) as built, accept F-1's trade, fix F-2 through F-11 and run round 2 -- the only option that leaves the common path exposed.
decisions.a: *** KENNETH CHOSE (3), 2026-09-22: KEEP GUARD (i) AS BUILT AT 4b273f22. DO NOT REVERT. Fix F-2 through F-11, then run ROUND 2. *** || HE WAS ASKED TO DISAMBIGUATE AND CONFIRMED IT: his answer read 'Lock (I)', which was ambiguous between card option 1 and guard (i) (the card numbered its options 1/2/3 without parens while this thread writes guards as (i)/(ii), and a standalone 'i' autocapitalises on mobile). He confirmed GUARD (i) -- card option 3. Recorded because the two readings are near-opposites and a wrong entry here is a wrong entry in the source of truth. || *** THE COST HE ACCEPTED, STATED PLAINLY SO NO LATER ROUND RE-LITIGATES IT AS A DISCOVERY: THE COMMON PATH IS KNOWINGLY LEFT MISMATCHED AFTER 16:00 ET. *** On the normal nightly-ingested (fresh-DB) path, a DB holding the previous session gives `last < min(end, _prev_trading_day())` -> `Tue < Tue` -> False -> NO BACKFILL, so the SCAN's series ends at the PREVIOUS session; meanwhile the GATE's feed asks Tradier with `end = date.today()` and after the close guard (i) KEEPS today's completed bar. Gate and scan then disagree by one bar, at the same 0.50%/0.92% flip rate and the same 'scan REJECT -> gate ABSTAIN -> FIRES UNGATED AT FULL ARMED QUANTITY' shape as the original F1. IN SESSION the guard trims and the common path MATCHES; the exposure is the post-close window only. The stale-DB case (a custom-universe name outside the SP500/NDX100/DOW30 prefetch, >=1 completed session behind) is the case guard (i) FIXES. || *** THE PREMISE CORRECTION IS PART OF THIS DECISION. AUTOTRADE-2B-CORE-F1-GUARD-I-SESSION-TEST-2026-09-21 still carries the sentence '(i) closes the narrow one without giving the common one back'. THAT SENTENCE IS FALSE and is marked false in place. Guard (i) decides FROM THE WALL CLOCK ALONE and never looks at the DB, so it cannot tell the two cases apart -- it TRADED the common case for the narrow one rather than closing both. Kenneth is keeping the trade with the arithmetic in view, which is not the same thing as the decision being right on its original reasoning. *** || VERIFIED AGAIN ON 2026-09-22 BEFORE THIS WAS WRITTEN, not carried over from the round's framing: historical_store.py:230 is `fetch_needed = (last is None) or (last < min(end, _prev_trading_day()))`; `most_recent_trading_day()` returns TODAY on a weekday and `_prev_trading_day()` is that minus one session; BOTH scan-side feeds reach it with `end = date.today()` -- routers/scan.py:1470-1483 (per-symbol bars) and routers/regime.py:329 (the regime series). The chain holds link by link. || GUARD (i)'S OWN LOGIC REMAINS VERIFIED SOUND and is NOT what was faulted: the session test is correct at every instant on the default path, the two-clause shape (session-open OR pre-09:30) holds, DST is right across both 2026 US flips, and round 3's defect is not reintroduced. The fault was the QUESTION IT ANSWERS, not its answer. || WHAT ROUND 2'S FIX MUST INCLUDE, because these are the reason F-1 got through at all: F-2 -- every test exercising the trim replaces `_todays_bar_is_unclosed` with a MagicMock, so the CALL SITE is unpinned and TWO CALL-SITE MUTANTS RESTORE THE ORIGINAL F1 AND PASS ALL 2787 TESTS. F-4 -- the new acceptance test is a TAUTOLOGY over the gate's own filter and never models `fetch_needed`, the one fact that decides the question. A test that cannot fail is not evidence. Fix those two first; a round 2 run against tests that mock away the wiring would repeat round 1. Then F-3, F-5 through F-7 (F-5: the host-ahead limb's 'those are post-close hours' holds only for hosts <= +8h from New York), and F-8 through F-11 (comment overstatements). || *** THE STAMP STAYS RECORDED AND NOT TAKEN. *** Stamping the scan's regime-series end date onto the armed card and trimming to THAT dissolves F1 and F-1 instead of trading them, and deletes the wall-clock helper. It is the snapshot rule (AUTOTRADE-ARMED-TRADE-JUDGED-BY-ITS-SCANS-RULE-2026-09-21) applied to the DATA axis instead of the CONFIG axis. IT TOUCHES THE ARM PATH, so it belongs to the SNAPSHOT TARGET, not the measurement core -- per AUTOTRADE-SNAPSHOT-FIX-GETS-ITS-OWN-TARGET-2026-09-21. Choosing (3) did NOT reject the stamp; it declined to let it into THIS target's diff. When the snapshot target is built, the stamp SUPERSEDES guard (i) and the post-close exposure above closes with it. DO NOT TAKE IT UNPROMPTED INSIDE THE CORE. || COUNTERS UNCHANGED BY THIS DECISION: MEASUREMENT-CORE r=1 not clean, CAP 1 OF 3, round 2 is the next round and is scoped to guard (i)'s own code and tests. IF THIS TARGET REACHES THREE ROUNDS WITHOUT A CLEAN, that is not a fifth split to invent -- STOP AND TELL KENNETH.

decisions.q: The measurement core inherited Option A's F1 unfixed: the end-trim justifies itself with 'on the fire path the market is PROVABLY OPEN', which is false -- `_market_is_open` is a price-availability probe, not an hours test, and neither fire path has an hours gate. So after 16:00 ET the gate drops a COMPLETED bar. Two guards were named and neither taken: (i) make the end-trim conditional on a real MARKET_TZ session test, (ii) keep the unconditional trim and drop the false premise, restating the residual honestly.
decisions.a: *** PREMISE CORRECTION 2026-09-22, DO NOT READ THIS RECORD WITHOUT IT: THE SENTENCE BELOW READING 'Option A fixed the common case and broke a narrower one; (i) closes the narrow one without giving the common one back' IS FALSE. Round 1 falsified it at historical_store.py:230 and the chain was re-verified on 2026-09-22. Guard (i) reads the WALL CLOCK ALONE and never looks at the DB, so it cannot distinguish the two cases: after 16:00 ET it KEEPS today's bar on BOTH paths, which is right for the stale-DB case and WRONG for the common nightly-ingested one, where the scan's series ended at the previous session. (i) TRADED the common case for the narrow one. Kenneth kept guard (i) anyway with that cost in view -- see AUTOTRADE-2B-CORE-GUARD-I-KEPT-COMMON-PATH-COST-ACCEPTED-2026-09-22, which is the operative decision now. Everything else in this record still stands, including the shape-of-the-fix constraint and the three-round stop. *** || *** KENNETH CHOSE (i), 2026-09-21: MAKE THE END-TRIM CONDITIONAL ON A REAL SESSION TEST. *** || THE DEFINITION: today's bar is dropped ONLY WHILE THE SESSION IS STILL OPEN. Once the session has closed, today's bar is COMPLETE and is KEPT. The test must be a real MARKET_TZ session-hours test -- `strategy_watch_scheduler.py:24` already does exactly this, so it is existing machinery rather than new, and the implementation should reuse it rather than hand-roll a second one. `_market_is_open` MUST NOT be used for this: it is a PRICE-AVAILABILITY probe (fetch_price serves close/previous_close around the clock, market.py:464/:474/:479) and its own docstring says the market 'APPEARS open'. That confusion is the whole defect. || WHAT IT FIXES, with the measured number: 0.50% of Position fires flip today, including scan PASS -> gate ABSTAIN, and AN ABSTAIN FIRES UNGATED AT FULL ARMED QUANTITY. That is the path this guard closes -- a trade going out at full size on a setup the scan refused. || THE NUANCE THAT MUST SURVIVE INTO THE ROUND, because losing it would make the fix look like a regression repair rather than a trade: OPTION A IS A NET IMPROVEMENT, NOT A REGRESSION. `get_bars` backfills only when `last < min(end, _prev_trading_day())`, so with the DB FRESH -- the normal nightly-ingested case -- the scan never sees today's bar either and Option A MATCHES, where the PRE-DIFF code did not. The mismatch needs the symbol's stored history to be >=1 completed session BEHIND: a custom-universe name, newly added, outside the SP500/NDX100/DOW30 prefetch. Option A fixed the common case and broke a narrower one; (i) closes the narrow one without giving the common one back. || *** THE SHAPE OF THE FIX IS PART OF THE DECISION, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. The cap fired TWICE on this target's predecessor and every fix there grew the next finding -- but that came from an 835-LINE TARGET, not from the act of fixing. This target is ~670 with a fresh 1-3 budget. SO: (i) GOES IN AS A SMALL, SINGLE-PURPOSE DIFF -- the session test and nothing else -- as the measurement core's ROUND 1 SUBJECT. Do not bundle other cleanups into it. A tight diff is the shape that converges; a bundled one is the shape that fired the cap twice. *** || IF THIS TARGET REACHES THREE ROUNDS WITHOUT GOING CLEAN, that is NOT a fifth split to invent. STOP AND TELL KENNETH.

decisions.q: The snapshot rule is decided, but the fix touches files in NO existing target's `paths`: scanStore.ts and the scan-result shape on the frontend, `_resolve_regime_gate` in services/auto_trader.py on the backend. Which target owns it?
decisions.a: *** ITS OWN TARGET. Recommended by me and put to Kenneth on 2026-09-21 as 'unless you object'; he did not object and moved on. RECORDED AS MY CALL ON HIS NON-OBJECTION, NOT AS A DECISION HE MADE -- if that reading is wrong it is cheap to re-file before a round runs. *** || WHY NOT SPLIT IT ACROSS THE TWO EXISTING TARGETS: the arm door owns AutoTradeArm/** and lib/api.ts; the measurement core owns services/auto_trader.py. The snapshot fix spans BOTH halves -- freeze the thresholds with the scan result (frontend) AND freeze the resolved gate at arm (backend). Filing it in two places means NEITHER round ever sees the whole change, which is exactly how a scan-versus-fire disagreement goes unnoticed. That failure mode is the thing this entire piece of work exists to remove. || THE NEW TARGET'S `paths` MUST COVER, AND ITS ROUNDS' DIFFS BE LIMITED TO: frontend/lib/scanStore.ts (the `partialize` block and `setScanOverrides`), whatever carries the scan result's thresholds, frontend/components/organisms/AutoTradeArm/index.tsx (the submit-time read at ~:259), and backend/app/services/auto_trader.py's `_resolve_regime_gate` and the `arm()` site that would freeze the resolved dict. FRESH 1-3 CAP, counted from its own round 1. || THIS DOES NOT TOUCH THE ARM DOOR'S OWN STATE: its cap has NOT fired (1 of 3), its F1 is answered by the snapshot rule, and a round 2 remains available to it once the fix lands wherever it lands.

decisions.q: Arm-door round 1's F1: the Step-3 headwind thresholds the arm payload snapshots are read from a store slice that is neither persisted nor frozen with the scan result, so the rule the fire gate applies need not be the rule the card's scan ran under. Which rule should an armed trade be judged by -- the one its scan actually ran under, or whatever is currently sitting in Step 3?
decisions.a: *** KENNETH DECIDED 2026-09-21: AN ARMED TRADE IS JUDGED BY THE RULE ITS OWN SCAN RAN UNDER. SNAPSHOT, NOT LIVE-READ. *** || THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, so this is falsifiable rather than a slogan: FROM THE MOMENT A CARD EXISTS, THE THRESHOLDS THAT JUDGE IT CANNOT CHANGE. Editing Step 3, resetting Step 3 to defaults, reloading the page, or editing scoring_rules.yaml must all leave an already-armed trade judged by exactly the numbers its scan resolved. If any of those five actions can move the verdict, the rule is not implemented. || WHY, and the first reason is coherence rather than taste: OPTION A (decisions AUTOTRADE-2B-UNCLOSED-BAR-OPTION-A-2026-09-21) already chose scan-parity on the DATA axis -- the gate measures the series the scan measured. Judging by a different RULE than the scan used would re-open the identical disagreement one axis over: the data mismatch fixed, the config mismatch left standing. || SECOND: THE REFUSAL MESSAGE IS ONLY TRUE UNDER SNAPSHOT. It says 'the scan's own regime_gate rule drops this setup'. If the rule changed between arm and fire, that sentence is false -- the same class of wrong-statement-to-a-user that 2B round 3 found on the unclosed bar. || THIRD: NO SURPRISES WITH MONEY ATTACHED. Kenneth arms a trade, then tunes Step 3 for his NEXT scan. Under live-read that tuning silently re-judges the armed one. Disarming is one click and is the explicit action; a config edit quietly changing what fires is not. || THE STALENESS OBJECTION IS WEAK HERE AND WAS WEIGHED: arms expire at `max_arm_age_minutes` (30 today), so the rule can drift for at most half an hour. The case for live-read -- 'I tightened because the market turned, I want it to bite now' -- is served by disarming. || *** TWO GAPS THIS RULE CLOSES, AND THE SECOND WAS NOT IN F1. *** (1) F1's gap: the arm payload reads `useScanStore.getState().scanOverrides` AT SUBMIT TIME (AutoTradeArm/index.tsx:259), and that slice is NOT in scanStore's `partialize`, is written by a bare `set()` that never invalidates `scanResult`, and survives both a threshold edit and 'Reset to defaults'. THE THRESHOLDS MUST BE FROZEN WITH THE SCAN RESULT and the arm payload must read them from there -- from what the scan actually used, not from a live control. (2) READ OFF THE BACKEND THIS SESSION AND NOT PART OF F1: `_resolve_regime_gate(strategy)` overlays the arm snapshot onto `_load_regime_gate_config()`, which is re-read AT FIRE TIME. So the Step-3 half is frozen and the YAML half is not. Under this rule the RESOLVED gate is frozen at arm -- resolve once in `arm()`, carry the dict, and have the fire path read it. ArmedStrategy's own comment already argues this: 'a half-frozen pair is worse than a frozen one'. That argument extends to the base, not just to the pair. || A DETAIL THAT SHRINKS THE BLAST RADIUS, recorded so nobody over-scopes the fix: `regime_headwind_caution_pct` IS INERT ON THE FIRE PATH. Only `reject_pct` decides whether a fire is refused; caution emits a log line and carries no reliable size consequence. Freeze both anyway, for the half-frozen reason above, but the value at risk is `reject_pct` plus the YAML base. || *** THE FIX LIVES OUTSIDE AUTOTRADE-2B-ARM-DOOR'S PATHS -- it is in the scan store and the scan result's shape (gap 1) and in services/auto_trader.py (gap 2), neither of which is in that target's five paths. THE SCOPING IS THEREFORE AN OPEN QUESTION AND IS NOT ANSWERED HERE: whether this becomes its own target, joins the measurement core, or widens the arm door is KENNETH'S CALL, not to be taken unprompted. The arm door's cap has NOT fired (1 of 3), so a round 2 remains available whichever way it is scoped. ***

decisions.q: The one adversarial round owed on Option A ran and came back NOT CLEAN (F1: the end-trim's 'market is provably open' premise is false; ~0.5% fire/no-fire flips on post-close fires of symbols whose stored history is behind). decisions[1] pre-committed this outcome to (C), the fourth split, and said it was Kenneth's to take rather than to be taken unprompted. Take it?
decisions.a: *** KENNETH TOOK (C), 2026-09-21. THE FOURTH SPLIT IS EXECUTED. *** AUTOTRADE-SIZING-2B-PER-SYMBOL-MEASUREMENT is replaced by AUTOTRADE-2B-ARM-DOOR (~160 lines) and AUTOTRADE-2B-MEASUREMENT-CORE (~670). The split is BY AUDIT TARGET, NOT BY BRANCH -- no pushed history was rewritten -- and each target's `paths` list is its definition and the limit of its rounds' diffs. || THE COUNTERS RESET TO ZERO ON BOTH, deliberately: the four rounds ran against the combined target, which no longer exists, and carrying 4 forward would re-fire the cap on the first round of a target created precisely to converge. The four-round history, the twice-fired cap and F1 are recorded in both phase notes instead of in a number. || F1 IS INHERITED OPEN AND UNFIXED BY THE MEASUREMENT CORE. Kenneth chose the split over fixing it first -- fixing past a twice-fired cap is the exact fix-introduces-the-next-finding pattern that produced rounds 2, 3 and 4 here. The two guards are named in that phase's note; NEITHER IS CHOSEN and neither is to be taken unprompted. || THE ARM DOOR IS NOT MARKED CLEAN even though no finding ever landed in it across four rounds, because audit_rule (3) requires a ROUND that returns zero gate-level findings and incidental coverage inside an unconvergeable target is not that round. It needs ONE round scoped to its paths and should clear in it. || NEXT UNIT OF WORK: that arm-door round. It is the cheapest thing on the board and it moves the merge gate from four of six to five of seven. || IF THE MEASUREMENT CORE REACHES THREE ROUNDS WITHOUT GOING CLEAN, the cap will have fired a third time on this work and the answer is NOT a fifth split -- stop and tell Kenneth.

decisions.q: 2B's hard cap fired at round 3: the auto-trade gate decides on TODAY'S UNCLOSED BAR, which the scan that armed the card never saw, flipping fire/no-fire in up to 1.00% of position-Bearish cases and making the refusal message false in exactly those cases. Three options were put to Kenneth: (A) drop the unclosed bar, (B) keep it and drop the agreement-with-the-scan claim, (C) take the fourth split first.
decisions.a: *** KENNETH CHOSE (A), 2026-09-21. DROP THE UNCLOSED BAR. *** || THE DEFINITION, so nobody re-derives it: THE GATE MUST MEASURE THE SAME COMPLETED-BAR SERIES THE SCAN DID. The gate's candle window ENDS AT THE LAST FULLY COMPLETED TRADING DAY -- the same boundary `historical_store.get_bars` already uses via `_prev_trading_day()` -- instead of `fetch_candles`' `end=today`. After the fix the two series must share their newest bar as well as their oldest, on a live fire, during market hours. That is the acceptance test: not 'the gate is correct' but 'the gate's series and the scan's series are the same series'. || WHAT THIS BUYS: the clock-dependence dies. Whether an order fires stops depending on where the stock happens to trade at the instant the trigger lands. The fail-open abstain path stops being reachable by a +0.11% intraday tick on a setup the completed data REFUSED. And the refusal message ('the scan's own regime_gate rule drops this setup') BECOMES TRUE AGAIN, because the scan's rule is now what actually ran. || WHAT IT COSTS, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN GLOSSED: it REDEFINES 2B'S OWN PREMISE. 2B was 'measure the traded symbol freshly at fire time'; under A the gate deliberately DISCARDS the freshest bar available to it. The new premise is narrower and should be written into the phase's own description: MEASURE THE TRADED SYMBOL RATHER THAN THE INDEX -- which was always the real defect 2B existed to fix (SPX-versus-MSFT) -- ON THE SAME COMPLETED-BAR SERIES THE SCAN USED. The per-symbol half survives untouched; only the freshness half is given up, and it is given up because it was buying a 1-in-100 coin flip rather than information. || THE NETWORK CALL ON THE FIRE PATH IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY REMOVED BY THIS AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED AWAY: a completed-bar series may still need fetching if the store does not hold it. Whether A lets the fire path read the store instead of the network is an IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION FOR THE FIX, and if it does, say so as a measured result, not as a hope. || *** THE AUDIT BUDGET, AND THIS IS THE PART THE CAP STILL GOVERNS. Kenneth chose A over C, so THE TARGET IS NOT SPLIT and stays at ~835 lines. The cap has FIRED ONCE. The plan is: BUILD A, then run ONE adversarial round SCOPED TO A'S OWN DIFF ONLY (audit_rule (2) -- not the whole 2B surface, which rounds 1-3 have already been over). IF THAT ROUND IS CLEAN, 2B CLOSES. IF IT IS NOT CLEAN, THAT IS THE SECOND CAP SIGNAL ON THIS TARGET AND THE ANSWER IS (C), THE FOURTH SPLIT -- arm door ~160 lines, measurement core ~670. STOP AND TELL KENNETH AT THAT POINT; do not run a further round and do not take the split unprompted. *** || WHY A ROUND IS STILL OWED AT ALL, since A is a narrowing change: rounds 1 and 3 BOTH landed on the same class of defect -- a mismatch between the window the gate measures and the window the scan measured -- and round 3's finding was round 1's own fix amplified. A touches exactly that seam. It is the highest-prior-probability place for the next one, not the lowest. || ALREADY DONE AND PUSHED, not to be re-litigated: round 1's fix (252-bar tail vs the scan's ~306-bar window) and round 2's fix (that fix evicted the shared candle cache and moved a stop price on unrelated users' screens). Round 3 confirmed round 2's fix clean and wrote no code. Suite 2770 passed / 1 skipped.

decisions.q: 2B round 3: round 2's fix is clean, but the round found a gate-level defect -- the gate decides on TODAY'S UNCLOSED BAR while the scan measured completed bars, and at round 1's ~306-bar window that flips fire/no-fire. Three rounds, none clean. What now?
decisions.a: *** STOPPED. THE HARD CAP HAS FIRED AND THE RULE IS BEING FOLLOWED: audit_rule says a phase that reaches THREE rounds without going clean is evidence the batch is too big to audit, not that it needs a fourth round -- STOP AND TELL KENNETH. THE FINDING IS RECORDED AND NOT FIXED. NO ROUND 4, AND NO FIX, WITHOUT HIM. *** Full record in `autotrade_2b_round3_2026_09_21`. || WHAT KENNETH IS BEING ASKED, and it is a product question wearing a bug's clothes. `fetch_candles` asks for `end=today` so the gate carries today's IN-PROGRESS bar; `historical_store.get_bars` backfills only to `_prev_trading_day()`, 'the last FULLY COMPLETED trading day', so the scan's series stops at the previous session; and `fire()` only runs while the market is open, so the gate ONLY EVER sees that bar unclosed. Reproduced independently: up to 1.00% of position-Bearish cases flip fire/no-fire on that single bar, and a +0.11% intraday move was enough to turn a REJECT into an abstain -- which FIRES, at full armed quantity, on a setup the completed-bar series refused. || THE TWO OPTIONS ARE DIFFERENT PRODUCTS, NOT DIFFERENT PATCHES. (A) DROP THE UNCLOSED BAR so the gate measures the same completed-bar series the scan did: removes the clock-dependence and the asymmetry in one move, but redefines what 2B means by 'measure freshly at fire time', because the freshest data available would be deliberately discarded. (B) KEEP THE LIVE BAR AND STOP CLAIMING AGREEMENT WITH THE SCAN: then the refusal message ('the scan's own regime_gate rule drops this setup' -- demonstrably false in these cases) and the 'agreement with the scan' justification carrying ALL FIVE abstain branches both have to be restated. || WHY NOT JUST FIX IT: this phase has demonstrated the fix-introduces-the-next-finding pattern TWICE. Round 2 found a defect INSIDE round 1's fix (the cache eviction). Round 3's finding is one round 1's fix AMPLIFIED, by moving the window from 252 to ~306 where min_obs becomes reachable and the newest bar can cross the REJECT threshold instead of merely abstaining -- which is also WHY ROUND 2 MISSED IT: round 2 measured the one-bar effect at 150-251 bars, a length the gate no longer uses. A third unaudited fix past a fired cap is the exact pattern that kept Phase A at six rounds and Phase D at thirteen. || THE FOURTH SPLIT IS NOW THE LIVE LEVER: arm door (routers/auto_trade.py + lib/api.ts + AutoTradeArm, ~160 lines) separates cleanly from the measurement core (auto_trader.py + its tests, ~670). The cap fired on the combined target; the measurement core is where all three rounds' findings live. STILL KENNETH'S TO TAKE, not to be taken unprompted. || THE MERGE GATE IS UNCHANGED BY THIS: four of six targets clean (SIZING-1, 2A-GATE, 2A-ALERT, 2C); 2B is now CAPPED-NOT-CLEAN and SIZING-3 has not started.

decisions.q: 2B round 2 reviewed round 1's fix and found one gate-level defect IN THE FIX -- asking for 400 bars evicts and rewrites the shared candle cache, moving a stop price on an unrelated user's screen. What was done, and what does round 3 do?
decisions.a: FIXED, ROUND 2 SPENT, TARGET NOT CLEAN -- audit_rounds 2 of 3. ROUND 3 IS THE LAST OF THE CAP; if it does not come back clean, audit_rule says STOP AND TELL KENNETH, do not run a fourth. Full record in `autotrade_2b_round2_2026_09_21`. || THE SHAPE OF THIS ROUND IS THE POINT. Round 2 found NOTHING wrong with the original 2B change. It found a defect in the REPAIR -- exactly the pattern audit_rule (2) was rewritten to stop ('the feature was converging; the fixing was not'). The target is behaving as the rule predicts, which is an argument FOR the shrinking scope and AGAINST reopening the original diff in round 3. || THE FIX: the fire path snapshots `market._candles_cache` and restores it in a `finally`, so it reads the shared cache and never authors it. Cold is restored to cold. The restore cannot distinguish our write from a concurrent one and therefore restores on ANY change; the cost is a slightly older same-day series for one symbol, against a measured user-visible stop change on every fire. ROUND 3 SHOULD TEST THAT TRADE rather than assume it. || ONE OVERCLAIM IS NOW ON RECORD AND WAS NOT FIXED, because it is wording and wording is below the gate: the helper's docstring says the gate and the scan cover 'THE SAME TRADING DAYS'. During a live session they differ BY ONE BAR -- the DB stops at the previous session while `fetch_candles` carries today's in-progress bar. Round 2 measured that bar's effect under the shipped config and found it changes only PASS<->abstain and CAUTION<->abstain, all of which FIRE, so no fire/no-fire or user-number change could be shown. IF ROUND 3 DISAGREES AND CAN SHOW A FIRE/NO-FIRE FLIP FROM THAT ONE BAR, it is gate-level and the wording is the least of it. || THE FOURTH SPLIT (arm door ~160 vs measurement core ~670) is now MORE relevant, not less: the cap is one round from firing. It remains KENNETH'S TO TAKE, not to be taken unprompted.

decisions.q: 2B round 1 returned one gate-level finding: the fire path measured 252 bars while the scan measures ~306, and compute_omm flips verdicts on that difference. What was fixed, what was deliberately not, and what does round 2 do?
decisions.a: FIXED IN-BRANCH, ROUND 1 SPENT, TARGET NOT CLEAN -- audit_rounds 1 of a fresh 1-3. Full record in `autotrade_2b_round1_2026_09_21`. || WHAT WAS FIXED: `_fetch_scan_window_bars` now asks for 400 bars and trims BY DATE to the scan's ~441-day window, replacing `fetch_candles(symbol)`'s 252-bar default. By date and not by count because the two readers of the shared candle cache slice it differently.
